messages: mia: Quick heads-up — noticed a token-level latency spike starting ~08:10 UTC on /v1/generate. P95 for token emit jumped from ~22ms to ~48ms on small batches. perf-bot: incident: kernel-selection-regression detected for model: redwood-v1-small. metric: token_emit_p95 +118% vs baseline. oliver: I saw that too, looks correlated with a recent kernel config change rolled yesterday (auto-sel=v2). Sophie, did the kernel fallback logic change? sophie: yes, I tweaked fallback thresholds to prefer fp16-kernelA over int8-kernelC for quality reasons. I didn't expect such a latency hit. ry an: tagging @sophie — can you paste the exact config diff? sophie: diff is tiny: ```- kernel_auto_select: v1+fallbacks: [int8-kernelC] + kernel_auto_select: v2+fallbacks: [fp16-kernelA, int8-kernelC]``` mia: also noticed KV cache hit rate dropped ~6% for long-context requests at the same time. perf-bot: KV_cache_hit_rate dropped from 0.87 -> 0.81 for route /v1/generate:customer:prod. oliver: hm that could explain extra compute and latency — additional KV reloads + suboptimal kernel choice. mia: I captured a flamegraph from the runtime.prof during the spike. Attaching excerpt: ```CPU: 1000ms samples top: 1) forward_fp16_kernelA 42% 2) kv_cache_reload 15% 3) kernel_switch_overhead 12% 4) batching_loop_wait 8%``` sophie: kernel_switch_overhead is new — must be from forcing fp16 paths where session has int8 cached artifacts. ryan: are we doing on-the-fly quantization transmute? That would add overhead. sophie: no transmute; but we introduced a quick compatibility shim that reconstructs attention kernels at session start, added in v2. oliver: suggestion: temporarily set auto-sel back to v1 for the affected pool and run a canary with explicit kernel pinning to confirm. mia: I can patch the routing policy to pin /v1/generate:customer:prod -> kernel=v1 for next hour. perf-bot: action scheduled: pin kernels for pool gpu-pool-4 at 09:05 UTC. ryan: also about batching heuristics — since token-level latency rose, are we hitting worse batch size distribution? mia: yes, batch sizes shifted more to mid-sized (8-16) instead of many 1-4; that increases per-token latency on some kernels due to cache locality. oliver: can we update the batching heuristic to prefer grouping short sequences together? sophie: we have a change in the heuristic that tries to maximize GPU occupancy by mixing lengths. I can revert that for a route-specific override. mia: for telemetry, we need token-level breakdowns on the dashboard: separate spans for kernel-selection, kernel-init, kv-reload, batch-queue-time, and token-emit. ryan: agreed — current dashboard only shows overall token latency and kernel_exec. perf-bot: new metric proposal recorded: token_latency_spans = [kernel_selection_ms, kernel_init_ms, kv_reload_ms, batch_wait_ms, emit_ms]. oliver: can we tie cost per token to these spans? e.g., estimate GPU-ms consumed per span and apply per-region unit pricing so product teams can see unit economics per route. sophie: doable — runtime already emits exec_ms per kernel and memory footprint. We need a billing mapper to convert exec_ms->cost using sustained GPU price tables. mia: I'll file a quick RFC to add a per-route cost view that aggregates token-level costs and aligns with billing. ryan: one thing to watch: billing alignment must match the accounting pipeline (events are aggregated at minute granularity). We should emit both raw token events and minute-aggregates. sophie: on the perf regression debugging plan: 1) pin kernel auto-sel for prod pool (mia) 2) run canary with kernel_v1 and v2 pinned (oliver) 3) enable detailed span telemetry for 30m (mia/ryan) 4) revert batching heuristic change for the route (sophie) 5) run perf evals with same prompt sets (bench infra). ryan: also add a unit-econ dashboard tile: cost_per_generated_token (USD) with breakdown by span. mia: doing that — linking to an ad-hoc grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/sessions/kerneltokencosts (private). sophie: one more data point — quantized kernels (int8) have smaller kernel_init but worse emit_ms variance for mid-batches on older drivers. Maybe driver+cuda issue. oliver: open a ticket to test driver 535 vs 545 on a replica pool. mia: will schedule. perf-bot: note: regression window 08:10-08:42 UTC, affected ~3% of production traffic, increased cost-per-token by ~9% for that slice. ryan: if pin + heuristic revert lowers cost-per-token by >5% we should roll back v2 auto-sel. oliver: agreed. mia: I'll post update after 09:40 UTC once canary finishes. :thumbsup: sophie: thanks, debugging now.```
